To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of Ck4/Cdk2 complexes is accompanied by increased cyclin D expression, decreased association of CDKI with cyclin E/Cdk2 complexes, and increased Cdk2 threonine 16 phosphorylation.

estradiol treatment of MCF-7 cells leads to increased cyclin D and cyclin E mRNA and protein levels, and to increased cyclin E-CdK2 activity, which precedes the onset of DNA synthesis and is associated with increased phosphorylation of Cdc2 on Thr-160 and reduced CDK inhibitor (p21, p27) association with cyclin E-Cdc2.

estrogen-induced G1-S phase transition is accompanied by increased activity of cyclin E-cdk2 and Cdk4, which is associated with decreased CDK inhibitor binding and Cdk-activating kinase-dependent phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the cell cycle and the control of cell proliferation.
the role of the estrogen receptor (ER) and ER-mediated signaling pathways in the control of cell proliferation.
the molecular mechanisms of estrogen receptor (ER) action in breast cancer and the development of new strategies for breast cancer prevention and treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the early estrogen-mediated activation of both cyclins D1 and E-Cdk4/Cdk2 complexes is due to a combination of both CDK inhibitor dissociation and CDK-activated kinase-mediated phosphorylation.
estrogen-induced cell cycle progression involves the sequential activation of both Cdk 4 and Cdk 2 complexes.
estrogen-induced activation of cyclin/cyclins and Cdk/cyclins is accompanied by increased expression of cyclins and decreased association of CDK inhibitors with cyclin E-Cdks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
estrogen-induced activation of Cdk2 is a consequence of increased expression of cyclin D1 and reduced association of CDK inhibitors.
estrogen-induced activation of Cdk2 is a complex process that involves both CDK inhibitor dissociation and Cdk2 activation by Cdk-activating kinase, but not increased Cdk2 expression.
estradiol stimulates cell cycle progression in MCF-7 cells by inducing the expression of cyclin D1 and cyclin E and by activating cyclin D1-associated Cdk4 and the cyclin E-associated Cdk2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of cyclin D-Cdk4 and of cyclin E-CDK2 is a prerequisite for the activation of cyclins A and B.
the activation of cyclin D1–Cdk4 is a primary event in estrogen signaling and that this is followed by the activation of cyclins E and A.
the estrogen-induced activation of cyclin D1/Cdk4 and cyclins E/Cdk2 complexes that occur during G1 phase are not due to a general increase in CDK activity.
